title: How do you give and take a compliment?
examples: How do I give someone a nice compliment?
What do I say when someone compliments me?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: The more specific, the more special it feels

explain.say: Imagine your friend shows you a dragon drawing. You could say, nice. Or you could say something that makes their face light up. Look at the left side of the board: an okay compliment. Nice, cool picture. Quick and general.

draw.text: How do you give and take a compliment?

explain.say: Now look at the right side: a great compliment. The colours in your dragon pop! It is specific, which means it names exactly what you like. It is true, and it can be about effort or kindness. Can you make one up?

explain.say: Now the other side: taking a compliment. Meet Sofia. Her teacher says her story had a brilliant ending. See her confused face? She nearly shrugs and says, it was nothing.

faq.q: How do I give a good compliment?
faq.a: Make it specific and true: name exactly what you like, like: Your dragon's colours really pop! Compliments about effort and kindness are extra special.
asks: Tell me about the Great compliment

faq.q: How should I take a compliment?
faq.a: Smile and say thank you. You can add something small, like: I worked hard on it. Try not to say it was nothing.
asks: What do I say when someone compliments me?

faq.q: Why is a specific compliment better?
faq.a: It shows you really noticed, so it feels real and special, not like something you say to everyone.
asks: Tell me about the Okay compliment

faq.a: They can be nice, but compliments about effort, ideas and kindness often mean more, because they are about who someone is and what they did.
asks: Should I compliment how people look?

faq.a: Being noticed and appreciated makes our brains feel happy and helps friendships grow, for the giver and the receiver.
asks: Why do I feel happy when someone praises me?

facts: A 2021 study by Xuan Zhao and Nicholas Epley found people underestimate how good their compliments make others feel.
World Compliment Day is celebrated on 1 March.
